articles.title: France: Trade unions join students in major demonstration
articles.summary: Tens of thousands are expected at nationwide protests against poor learning conditions for students in France.

image.caption: Rights groups have accused the police of using disproportionate force on children.Image: Raphael Lafargue/abaca/picture alliance

blocks.text: A day of nationwide blockades and street protests are planned on Tuesday in France, led by high-school and trade union groups. Tens of thousands are expected to take to the streets.
The demonstrations are part of a movement that sprung in recent weeks demanding that french President Emmanuel Macron's government tackle understaffed and underfunded schools.
Protests that began in Paris's deprived suburbs have now spread across the country, including pupils from affluent areas who have joined in solidarity.

Hundreds of high school entrances have been blocked by student protesters since late September. The students have decried poor learning conditions, such as missing teachers, overloaded timetables, dilapidated classrooms and buildings that are not suitable for high temperatures.

While many of the demonstrations have been peaceful, some protesters have lit trash can fires, destroyed bus shelters or clashed with riot police, who have responded with batons, tear gas and riot-control rounds, with authorities accusing the movement of having devolved into urban violence.

blocks.caption: Rights groups have accused the police of using disproportionate force on children.Image: Raphael Lafargue/abaca/picture alliance

blocks.text: Police accused of brutality towards children
The country's Justice Ministry said that 5,060 people have been arrested since the protests began. Some 87% of those taken into custody were minors.
Over 1,800 people face charges, including 1,483 minors, the ministry said, without ​providing details of what they had been accused of, although some 790 cases have alaready been dismissed.

Trade unions and human rights groups have accused the police of using disproportionate force on children. Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said on Monday that police have launched 10 internal investigations into allegations of brutality since the protests started.

Among the reports, a 15-year-old lost his hand at a protest in the northern town of Lens, a 16-year-old lost the use of his right eye after being seriously injured in the head in the central town of Tours, while in Saint-Ouen-L'Aumone, northwest of Paris, a 14-year-old lost most of his teeth when a police officer appeared to fire a projectile at him at very close range.

blocks.caption: Students have demanded that the governmetn improve learning conditionsImage: Raphael Lafargue/abaca/picture alliance

blocks.text: Government promises response
French Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu said he had ‌ordered government ministers to study the students' leading demands.
Among the demands the government will be tackling are ensuring absent teachers are replaced, reviewing the ‌length ​of the 8 a.m. to 6 p.m. school day and the need for longer lunch breaks.
The government has promised to also look at repairs needed to ageing school buildings.
Lecornu said ministers are expected to submit their first proposals by the end of October. The ​protests have put pressure on a government that has sought to narrow a ballooning budget deficit.

articles.title: Kenya confirms its first Ebola death as outbreak spreads
articles.summary: The patient has been living in DR Congo for the past seven years.

blocks.text: Kenya has confirmed its first case of Ebola - a Kenyan citizen who has been living in the Democratic Republic of Congo for the past seven years.
Health Minister Aden Duale said the patient, who fell ill a month ago, and was treated in several hospitals in DR Congo, died days after arriving in Nairobi.

Duale said the patient boarded a flight on Saturday and underwent normal public screening at the main airport in Nairobi before he was transferred by a relative to a hospital in the city. Tests conducted confirmed positive for Ebola Bundibugyo virus.
More than 4,000 people have died from Ebola in DR Congo this year, in what is the second most deadly known outbreak of the disease.

articles.title: Sara Duterte says her father Rodrigo still remembers her
articles.summary: Vice President Sara Duterte on Tuesday disputed claims that her father, former President Rodrigo Duterte, who is detained in The Hague, Netherlands, over crimes against humanity charges, had…

blocks.text: Published October 6, 2026 4:44pm

Vice President Sara Duterte on Tuesday disputed claims that her father, former President Rodrigo Duterte, who is detained in The Hague, Netherlands, over crimes against humanity charges, had forgotten her.
Speaking at a press conference in Davao City, Duterte said her father recently called her, dismissing claims that the 81-year old former president could no longer remember his children.
“Yes, forgetful si PRRD, pero tumawag siya sa akin nung… bago lang. So hindi niya ako nakalimutan. Sinabihan ko siya, bakit ngayon ka lang tumawag sa akin. Ang tagal mo nang hindi tumawag,” she said.
(Yes, PRRD is forgetful, but he called me just recently. So he has not forgotten me. I told him, why are you only calling me now? It’s been so long since you last called me.)
Over the weekend, former presidential spokesperson Harry Roque claimed that Duterte could no longer determine the passage of time or recall the names of his children and grandchildren.
The claim comes as Duterte’s defense team continues to challenge his fitness to stand trial before the International Criminal Court (ICC), citing alleged cognitive and memory problems.
The ICC has ordered an updated assessment of Duterte’s fitness for the trial phase, after an earlier assessment found him fit to participate in pretrial proceedings.
According to the vice president, her father told her during their call, “Wala lang. Nangamusta lang ako sa imoha.”
(He said, ‘Nothing. I just wanted to check on you’.)
“Sabi niya ikaw kasi ang tumawag sa akin,” she said.
(He said, “You should be the one to call me.”)
Duterte said she explained to her father that she could not call him directly and that he had to ask the authorities at his detention facility to connect him to her.
“Sabi ko, hindi nga kasi pwede. Dapat ikaw ang magsabi doon sa—diyan sa loob na tawagan mo ako. Kasi hindi man kami maka-dial, makatawag doon papasok. Pwede lang palabas siya tumawag,” she added.
(I said, “No, because it’s not possible. You have to tell those inside there to call me. Because we can’t dial or make calls to them. He can only make outgoing calls.”)
Duterte said she did not tell her father about what was happening to her.

“Actually, wala namang nangyayari sa akin. Political lang naman lahat ang nangyayari. Sinabi ko lang sa kanya na bibisita ako sa ganito na dates, okay lang ba sa’yo. Sabi niya sige, okay na ’yan,” she said.
(Actually, nothing is happening to me. Everything that is happening is just political. I just told him that I would visit on these dates, is that okay with you? He said, “Sure, that’s okay.”)

Duterte is facing an impeachment trial over allegations that she made grave threats against President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. and others, misused confidential funds, had unexplained wealth and engaged in bribery.
She is also facing three counts of grave threats before a Quezon City court.

In September, dismissed policeman Rodulfo Gracioso Jr. claimed that he delivered cash to Sara Duterte, Davao City 1st District Rep. Paolo Duterte and the former President Rodrigo Duterte, allegedly on the instructions of former House Speaker Lord Allan Velasco.

Meanwhile, Rodrigo Duterte is facing crimes against humanity charges before the ICC in connection with killings linked to his war on drugs when he was mayor of Davao City and later when he was president.— MCG, GMA News

articles.summary: Senator-judge Robin Padilla said Tuesday he never received even a single centavo from China or Chinese entities, as he admitted being linked to an alliance that supposedly received P150 million from…

blocks.text: Published October 6, 2026 4:33pm

Senator-judge Robin Padilla said Tuesday he never received even a single centavo from China or Chinese entities, as he admitted being linked to an alliance that supposedly received P150 million from the country.

On the Day 34 of the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte, Padilla asked that the Tapang at Malasakit Alliance for the Philippines no longer be dragged in the issue as alleged by former senator Antonio Trillanes IV.

"Sana po masabi lang doon sa ating mga kasama na, tutal hindi naman nabanggit dito 'yung sa Tapang at Malasakit, hinihingi ko po na 'wag naman kaming madamay lahat. Kasi kasama kami diyan eh. Hindi naman po 'yan nabanggit dito sa korte. Binanggit 'yan ni former senator Trillanes na hindi sa korteng ito," Padilla said.

(I hope the parties realize that since the Tapang at Malasakit was not initially mentioned here in the trial, I ask that we not all be implicated. Because we are part of that alliance. It wasn't brought up here in the trial. It was former senator Trillanes who mentioned it, but not in this court.)
"So hinihiling ko lang po sa mga kasama ko na pagka-gineralarize po natin 'yan na Tapang at Malasakit, kasama po kami diyan. Wala po akong natanggap na pera kahit na singko sa mga Intsik,” he added.
(So, I just want to ask the parties to consider that when we generalize the Tapang at Malasakit, they’re reminded that we are included in that. I never received a single cent from the Chinese.)

To recall, Trillanes claimed that Cale88 Foods Corporation and Tapang at Malasakit Alliance for the Philippines Inc., which were declared assets of Duterte in her joint SALN with her husband, lawyer Mans Carpio, received P319 million and P150 million, respectively, from the Chinese government and firms.

In 2017, then-Davao City mayor Duterte led the launching of the Tapang at Malasakit Alliance for the Philippines in support of the administration of her father, former president Rodrigo Duterte. — VDV, GMA News

articles.title: Negros Trade Fair 2026 doubles last year’s attendance at SMX Aura
articles.summary: SM and ANP welcomed nearly 80,000 visitors to BÚTLAK, setting a new benchmark for the Negros Trade Fair in Manila.

items: The 40th Negros Trade Fair attracted nearly 80,000 visitors, doubling last year's attendance.
The event generated nearly P118 million in sales, with P75 million from spot sales, indicating strong consumer demand, particularly in the food section where many exhibitors sold out early.
The fair highlighted a blend of heritage and innovation, with established brands and younger entrepreneurs presenting fresh takes on traditional products.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

Editor’s note: This press release is sponsored by SM Supermalls and was handled by BrandRap, the sales and marketing arm of Rappler. No member of the news and editorial team participated in the publishing of this piece.

BÚTLAK: The 40th Negros Trade Fair welcomed 79,512 visitors to SMX Convention Center Aura from September 22 to 27—double last year’s attendance and the highest foot traffic recorded in the fair’s Manila run. Organized by the Association of Negros Producers (ANP), in partnership with SM Supermalls through SM for MSMEs, and the Provincial Government of Negros Occidental, the six-day fair brought together 126 exhibitors across 177 booths. Visitors came to explore the food, fashion, crafts, home finds, and travel stories of the Negros Island Region—and left with more than a few bags in hand.

blocks.caption: A TASTE OF NEGROS. From pantry staples and artisanal preserves to freshly made delicacies, visitors filled their bags with food finds that carried the flavors and stories of Negros beyond the fair.

blocks.text: BÚTLAK generated nearly P118 million in reported sales, based on submissions from 120 exhibitors, with six reports still being consolidated. Of this amount, P75 million came from spot sales, a 39% increase year on year and a strong indicator of direct consumer demand. Another P43 million came from business-to-business transactions involving institutional buyers, retailers, distributors, and other partners.

blocks.caption: ONE BITE AT A TIME. From comforting bowls and smoky grilled favorites to sweet local treats, BÚTLAK gave visitors a delicious way to experience the region’s rich culinary heritage.

blocks.text: The strong sales were evident in the food section, where several exhibitors—including Cocina Javellana, Bacolod Chicken House, and Wawa Bing’s Kitchen—sold out as early as the second day. Many food booths had also run through their inventory by late afternoon.

Among the fair’s crowd favorites were Bacolod Chicken House’s inasal 21’s batchoy, Vaca Japonesa’s Wagyu Kansi and Wagyu Tapa N Rice; Wawa Bings Kitchen’s fresh lumpia; Cocina Javellana’s ube halaya; Felicia’s ensaymada and El Ideal’s freshly made hot piaya. Visitors also sought out Ading’s Gourmet Kitchen’s batuan fruit paste, blue crab paste, and smoked bangus; Ereñeta-Manaloto Chorizo de Bacolod; Nanette’s VCO, coco cider vinegar, and sinamak; and Filipino favorites from Imay’s Bar & Restaurant. The results point to a clear opportunity for future editions: helping exhibitors prepare more inventory and production capacity to meet growing demand.

BÚTLAK’s strongest stories came from the meeting of legacy and new energy. Heritage brands continued to draw loyal customers, while younger founders and next-generation family members gave familiar products a fresh look, new flavors, and a stronger connection with today’s shoppers.

Bob’s, one of Bacolod’s most established food names, reintroduced itself through a retro-inspired Bob’s Sari-Sari Store concept, with members of the third generation helping man the booth. El Ideal, the heritage bakery founded in 1920, remained a crowd-drawer for its hot piaya while also attracting curiosity for its Guapple Pie. “We have been around for about 100 years because we never sacrificed quality,” said Maritess Sanchez of El Ideal. “The Negros Trade Fair has helped us expand our reach here in Manila.” The fair also made room for a newer generation of makers.

Upcycled by The Little Vintage Shop gave donated clothing a second life through circular fashion, while LAKAT featured locally made footwear incorporating pineapple-based textiles and other Philippine natural materials. NVC Foundation’s Artisans of Hope showcased handmade mosaic pieces that support Bacolod-based artisans, while Alter Trade Philippines connected shoppers to fair-trade products that support Negros sugarcane producers and rural livelihoods.

blocks.caption: FOR MSMEs. ANP president Christina Gaston spotted at the Negros Trade Fair.

blocks.text: “For ANP, MSME development is about giving people the opportunity to discover what they can create, what they can become, and where their creativity can take them,” said ANP president Christina Gaston.“Over 40 years, we have seen small businesses grow into enterprises and local products reach markets once thought beyond their reach.”

blocks.caption: DISCOVERING THE DETAILS. Shoppers browsed handwoven textiles, handcrafted bags and contemporary apparel, connecting directly with the artistry and stories woven into every Negrense creation.

blocks.text: The celebration opened with Arima, the symbolic ringing of the bell that traditionally marks the start of the workday—and, for BÚTLAK, the festive opening of Negros in Manila. At the heart of the annual ritual is food: an invitation for guests to experience Negrense ingredients, heritage and hospitality at the table.

This year, Manila chefs brought contemporary flair to familiar flavors and ingredients sourced from participating exhibitors. Negrense chef Don Colmenares of destination restaurant Sauma served Kansi Croquetas with Negros beef, batuan mayo and langka purée, alongside an Atcharang Ukoy with dilis polvoron, sinamak mayo and malunggay pesto.

Chef Luis Locsin presented his signature Negrense-inspired pâté en croûte creations: a Pork and Native Chicken Mosaic Pâté en Croûte with native chicken, Victorias ham, dried fruits, almonds and Don Papa Rum; and a Pork and Duck Pâté en Croûte with Victorias bacon, oyster mushrooms, herbs and port wine. Chef Cara Davis of Halong created a Saravia Coconut Crab Lumpia, served with coconut chutney, atchara, fermented garlic, kiwot honey and Vietnamese green chili sauce.

Official caterer Epicura, the catering arm of Curio led by Pia Lago and chef Bettina Arguelles, completed the spread with KBL rillette on oat thins, seasonal seafood kinilaw with tultul salt, crab bibingka with calcag dust and bihod, corned beef kansi with kansi gravy, pancit luglug molo, and pork bellychon with batuan chimichurri.

New to this year’s Arima, private chef Bea Magalona reimagined familiar favorites through an Adobarquillo—barquillos filled with Ilonggo-style adobo cream—and Piaya Toast, made with langka piaya, kadyos hummus and pork. Together, the Arima menu showed how the flavors of Negros can remain rooted in heritage while finding fresh expression through a new generation of chefs and culinary collaborators.
For SM Supermalls, BÚTLAK demonstrates how access to the right marketplace can help local businesses reach more customers and create new opportunities for growth.

blocks.caption: SM Supermalls’ executive vice president for marketing Joaquin San Agustin.

blocks.text: “Every purchase does more than bring home a piece of Negros,” said Joaquin L. San Agustin, executive vice president for marketing at SM Supermalls, during the opening. “It supports a local business, celebrates Filipino creativity, and helps another entrepreneurial story move forward.”

blocks.caption: CREATIVE COMMUNITY VISITS. Familiar faces from fashion, food, design and entertainment joined shoppers at BÚTLAK, exploring the people, products and stories that made the 40th Negros Trade Fair a standout Manila gathering.

blocks.text: Through SM for MSMEs, SM Supermalls works with partners such as ANP to help open doors for homegrown businesses—connecting them to shoppers, visibility, and bigger opportunities to grow. With nearly 80,000 visitors and nearly ₱118 million in reported sales, BÚTLAK’s milestone edition showed that when local products are given room to be discovered, the impact reaches far beyond the fair itself. It creates new possibilities for the people, families, and communities behind every product. BÚTLAK: The 40th Negros Trade Fair was organized by the Association of Negros Producers in partnership with SM Supermalls and the Provincial Government of Negros Occidental. — Rappler.com

articles.title: Escudero: Sara Duterte, husband's total net worth doesn't match bank transactions
articles.summary: The total net worth of Vice President Sara Duterte and her husband, Manases Carpio, as stated in their joint Statement of Assets, Liabilities, and Net Worth (SALN) from 2002 to 2025 does not match…

blocks.text: Published October 6, 2026 4:28pm

The total net worth of Vice President Sara Duterte and her husband, Manases Carpio, as stated in their joint Statement of Assets, Liabilities, and Net Worth (SALN) from 2002 to 2025 does not match the millions of bank transactions under their name, Senate impeachment court presiding officer Francis Escudero said Tuesday.

At the same time, Escudero said that the P4.4 billion of covered and suspicious bank transactions from 2007 to 2025 recorded under the couple's name do not match their joint SALN declarations covering the same period.
Escudero made the observation based on the testimony of Anti-Money Laundering Council Executive Director Ronel Buenaventura before the Senate impeachment court

“P424 million ang pumasok at lumabas sa bank accounts ni Vice President Duterte at ng kanyang asawa from 2022 to 2025. I try to bring things in its absurd possibility to find out and test the hypothesis. In-add ko iyong SALN ng Pangalawang Pangulo mula 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025. Hindi naman dapat i-add ‘yun kasi iba’t ibang taon. [Pero] in total, P336 million. Hindi pa rin umabot ng P424 million,” Escudero said during Day 34 of the impeachment trial of Duterte.
(P424 million inflows and outflows from 2025 to 2025. I added the SALN from 2022 to 2025. Actually, you cannot add it but even so, the total is P336 million. It won't reach P424 million.)
“Meaning to say, on the assumption na walang ginastos mula sa lahat na assets nila at lahat na dineposit sa bangko, hindi pa rin aabot sa ganiting kalaking halaga,” he added.
(Even if they left their entire assets untouched and just deposited them all in banks, it won't reach that amount.)

Escudero said the case is the same for the P4.4 billion worth of covered and suspicious bank transactions under the names of Vice President and her husband from 2007 to 2025 when compared with SALNs for the same period.

“Yung P4.4 billion covering the period 2007 to 2025. Again, I bring it to its absurd point. We tried to add to all of the amounts in the combined SALNs for those covered period of 2007 to 2025. It totaled only P840 million,” he said.
“You would need five times at least five times of the combined SALN [net worth] total from 2007 to 2025 to be able to explain the huge amount of P4.4 billion in [bank] transactions,” he added.
In both instances, Escudero asked Buenaventura what would be the possible arithmetic that would match the SALN declarations with bank transactions.
“Can you explain how it could reach that amount knowing that the highest SALN in 2025 was at P98 million and the lowest SALN in 2007 was at P7 million? Can you explain it, Sir,” he said.
Buenaventura replied, “I am unable to explain or answer that, Your Honor.”
Escudero pressed, “But in the realm of possibilities, is there a possible explanation that can come to your mind as to how this can be? If you know.”
The AMLC official responded by saying, “On top of my head, nahihirapan po ako. Apologies po. I cannot explain it (It is really tough to explain).” —AOL, GMA News

articles.title: Badenoch denies ‘British Iron Dome’ plan – after Tories use phrase in press release
articles.summary: Tory leader says proposed ‘Britannia Shield’ will not be comparable to Israeli missile defence system

blocks.text: Kemi Badenoch has denied she compared a new air defence system proposed by the party to Israel’s Iron Dome, despite using the term in her press release and a newspaper article.
The Conservative leader said the party’s proposed “Britannia Shield” would not be comparable to the missile defence system in Israel, which is primarily designed to counter short-range attacks.

The party has proposed allotting £1bn a year towards building the system, though the former army general Richard Barrons told Times Radio the cost of a system similar to Israel’s would be upwards of £100bn.
Badenoch said on Times Radio it was a “semantic argument” and that the new system would protect Britain from increasing threats.
She told BBC Radio 4’s Today programme that the description had come from newspapers – though the Conservative party press release described the system as “in essence a British Iron Dome”.

In a piece authored by Badenoch in the Sun, which illustrated its front page with an image of Israel’s Iron Dome, she wrote: “Modelled on Israel’s ‘Iron Dome’, Britannia Shield will invest £10bn over 10 years in the radar, missiles and technology needed to detect these threats and stop them before they reach British soil.”

But Badenoch told Today that was not the aim. “We are not building the Iron Dome. We are doing what other European countries are doing: Greece, Benelux countries – Belgium and the Netherlands – and Germany. We are designing something specific for the kind of threat that we face here.”
Asked why newspapers had chosen to describe it as an Iron Dome, Badenoch said: “You’ll have to speak to the newspapers about that. I called it the Britannia Shield.

“But we are explaining to people that missile defence systems are things that we need right now. The Iron Dome is one type, and we want people to understand what we’re talking about, we haven’t said that we are replicating that. And the money that we are spending, £1bn a year over 10 years, should be able to deliver this.”

The shadow defence secretary, James Cartlidge, likened the phrase “iron dome” to the vacuum cleaner brand name Hoover when he was asked why Badenoch had denied the Conservatives were proposing an Iron Dome-style system.

He told journalists: “So, the phrase ‘iron dome’ has come to be used a bit like the word ‘hoover’ to generically refer to missile defence systems – and this is clearly a missile defence system. Is it the exact same iron dome as Israel? No.

“The Israeli Iron Dome is a short-range system. It’s to do with very near threats from the likes of Hezbollah. It was actually originally designed for artillery and very unsophisticated weaponry, whereas what we’re talking about, Britannia Shield, is a bespoke UK system. It’s just, if you speak to the media and the public, if you say ‘iron dome’ they at least know roughly what you’re talking about.”

blocks.caption: Part of Israel’s Iron Dome air defence system near Jerusalem in 2024. Photograph: Menahem Kahana/AFP/Getty Images

blocks.text: Cartlidge will say later at the Tory party conference that the UK needs to be ready to defend itself from potential aerial attacks and that new investment is needed in advanced radar and interceptor missiles.

Asked on Times Radio if the aim was to be able to intercept any attack over the entire country, Badenoch said: “It should, but it needs to protect critical national infrastructure … Critical national infrastructure protects the entire country. If we lose even one thing, the entire country is in a real problem, and that’s what we mean.”

Badenoch will give her own speech to close the conference on Wednesday. Asked whether she was ready for an election, Badenoch told Today she believed polls would improve but she admitted the party was still unpopular because of the previous government, even though her personal popularity had improved.

“I think people still associate the Conservative party with the things they didn’t like about the previous government,” she said. “I need to work hard to change that … these things take time. I am the leader and I need to show that this party is different from the party that the people said no to two years ago.
“I am confident that when that election is called, people will see that the Conservative party has the best offer. We have a strong team, we have a plan and we’re all about common sense.”

A Labour source said: “It’s no surprise Kemi Badenoch wants to forget how the Tories hollowed out our armed forces. But hoping her half-baked defence promise based on fantasy numbers will be forgotten just hours after it was made shows how unserious she is about our country’s security. The Tories can never be given responsibility for keeping Britain safe again.”

articles.title: NBI confirms Velasco couple owns 2 alleged ‘cash houses’ in Pasig
articles.summary: The NBI said Velasco spouses own 2 alleged “cash houses” in Pasig and are linked to 2 Marinduque resorts under investigation.

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Initial validations by the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) have confirmed that former House Speaker Lord Allan Velasco and his wife, Rowena, own two alleged "cash houses" in Pasig City, along with two beach resorts in Marinduque that are being probed for suspicious financial activities.

NBI Director Melvin Matibag said on Tuesday, October 6, that they have established the ownership following the claims of dismissed policeman Rodulfo Gracioso Jr. that Velasco and his wife bought properties to store large volumes of cash during the lawmaker’s term as House speaker.

“Basically, nitong mga nakaraang araw ang vinalidate natin ‘yung claim niya doon sa cash houses na sinasabi and we’re able to establish, dun sa seven cash houses na sinasabi, we’ve already established two that are owned by Velasco spouses,” Matibag said.

(Basically, these past few days, we validated his claims about cash houses, and we’re able to establish that among the alleged seven cash houses, we’ve already established two that are owned by Velasco spouses.)
Both houses were located in Valle Verde 2 in Pasig: one on Champaca Street, and another on Sampaguita Street, according to Matibag.
The NBI said investigators checked land titles and Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) records in validating the ownership.
'Cash houses'
In his affidavit, Gracioso claimed Velasco was the primary source and coordinator of multi-million-peso cash deliveries to Vice President Sara Duterte.
The cash, he claimed, came from the 25% “all-in” kickbacks on government projects across the country.

He said the cash was initially packed and stored at the residence of Velasco and his wife at No. 142 Sampaguita St., Valle Verde 2, but the money grew too large, which made the former lawmaker buy at least six additional houses where they could store the money.
Velasco and Duterte have earlier denied Gracioso’s claims.
The NBI said the established ownership of the two houses in Pasig by Velasco has so far supported Gracioso’s claims.

“Dun sa mga claims ni Mr. Gracioso ng bahay at pag-aari ng mga Velasco, tumatama na. Especially lalo na doon sa bahay because ‘yung bahay it was named under Eagle Assets and Realty na ang presidente nito si Ms. Rowena Velasco,” Matibag said.

(The claims of Mr. Gracioso on residences and properties are beginning to be validated. Especially on the houses, because the houses were named under Eagle Assets and Realty, whose president is Ms. Rowena Velasco.)
Resorts in Marinduque
Aside from the houses in Pasig, the NBI said it also looked into Gracioso’s claims that Velasco was investing a lot of money into two resorts at Poctoy White Beach in Torrijos, Marinduque.
Matibag said the Sara Resort and Cabanas and Amara Resort and Villas were both linked to the Velasco spouses.
“Napakalaking resort niyan. When we checked sa SEC ‘yung ownership, lumalabas na sa spouses Velasco. May mga inassign na na-share without consideration. So ini-investigate natin ‘yan,” Matibag said.
(That is a very big resort. When we checked the ownership on the SEC, it appears to belong to spouses Velasco. There were shares assigned without consideration. So we’re investigating that.)

NBI said the Sara Resort and Cabanas is operated by 888 Wealth Star Corp, where Rowena Velasco serves as president and chairman, holding 60% of the shares. The P20 million capital, the agency said, was reported to be fully paid in cash at incorporation.

The Amara Resorts and Villas, meanwhile, is operated by Amara Equity Ventures Inc., where Velasco and his wife were principal incorporators holding 80% of subscribed shares. The NBI said both transferred their original shareholdings to third parties in 2023, but Rowena remained a stockholder while serving as vice president.

The NBI said they are investigating the link between the two resorts as SEC records showed that the same individuals are serving as officers in both, while the incorporators share the same address. Individuals handling corporate filings for one resort also appeared on the records of the other.
Matibag said they will continue to investigate crucial documents to identify how these properties were acquired, who the owners are, and where the funds came from.

articles.title: Marcos in Singapore (again): A Forbes event… and an F1 Grand Prix
articles.summary: Marcos has visited the city-state several times before — two of those times, he attended the Singapore Grand Prix

RTVM Screengrab

items: President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. is visiting Singapore from October 7 to 11 to strengthen ties and promote economic engagement, following an invitation from Prime Minister Lawrence Wong.

During his visit, Marcos will participate in several events, including a meeting with Wong, the 24th Forbes Global CEO Conference, a visit to the Singapore Nuclear Research and Safety Institute, and the Formula 1 Singapore Grand Prix.

The trip coincides with the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte, and Marcos has defended his foreign trips as beneficial investments for the Philippines, aimed at attracting trade and strengthening diplomatic ties.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.
President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. is set to visit neighboring Singapore yet again from October 7 to 11, upon the invitation of Prime Minister and finance chief Lawrence Wong.

In a text briefing for the media, Department of Foreign Affairs (DFA) spokesperson Analyn Ratonel framed the visit as an “initiative of the [Philippines] to deepen ties with Singapore, expand economic engagement, and promote cooperation in sectors that would benefit the country.”
Singapore is also set to take over chairmanship of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) after Manila.
While in the city-state, Marcos is expected to engage in at least four major events:

items: Meeting with Wong
24th Forbes Global CEO Conference
A visit to the Singapore Nuclear Research and Safety Institute
The Formula 1 Singapore Grand Prix

blocks.text: It’s the last event that sticks out. After all, Marcos has been criticized for attending the same event twice — in 2022, barely months into his term and again in 2023. His latest Singapore Grand Prix attendance happened days after a speaking engagement with the Milken Institute.
Marcos has visited Singapore several times before, including the 2022 and 2023 visits that included a Grand Prix attendance.

This is how Ratonel explained Marcos’ expected attendance at the Singapore Grand Prix: “The President has been personally invited by Prime Minister Lawrence Wong to the Singapore Formula 1 Grand Prix. The Singapore Grand Prix brings together government leaders, business executives, and investors from around the world. It would provide an opportunity for informal engagements to complement his meetings focused on attracting investment and strengthening the Philippines’ partnerships.”

Aside from Wong, there are no other planned meetings for Marcos in Singapore. “However, there may be opportunities for the President to engage with leaders and senior officials, not just from Singapore, but from other countries, as well as business executives, during the Singapore Grand Prix,” said Ratonel in the briefer for media.

Marcos will be joined by Finance Secretary Frederick Go, Trade Secretary Cristina Aldeguer-Roque, and acting Communications Secretary Dave Gomez. Ratonel did not say whether First Lady Liza Araneta-Marcos would be part of the delegation, but she almost always joins the President in trips overseas.
The Philippine President is said to be fond of attending the Singapore Grand Prix — even amid turbulent times in Philippine domestic politics, it turns out.

His trip to Singapore coincides with the impeachment trial of erstwhile ally Vice President Sara Duterte which is at its arguably most controversial and contentious period — with the second-highest elected official of the land alleged of hiding her wealth and receiving money from the Chinese government through a business shared with her husband.

Marcos has distanced himself from these allegations, even as his alter-egos in the security and defense sector have called for further inquiries into allegations of financial ties between Duterte and Beijing.
Ratonel, in the prepared Q&A for media, echoed previous statements by the President in defending the quick Singapore sojourn.

“President Marcos has said that official foreign trips should be assessed based on their benefits to the country, not only on their cost. He has described these trips as investments that can help attract trade and investment, create jobs, strengthen security and diplomatic ties, and promote Philippine interests abroad,” she said. – Rappler.com

articles.title: UK events firm that hosts arms fairs and comic shows sold to rival for £2bn
articles.summary: FTSE 100 firm Informa to buy Clarion from private equity group Blackstone

blocks.text: A British events business that hosts arms fairs and conventions for comic book fans has been snapped up by a FTSE 100 rival for more than £2bn.
Informa has struck a £2.24bn deal to buy the London-based events organiser Clarion from the private equity group Blackstone

The takeover will add more than 100 events to Informa’s portfolio – from the defence and security exhibit DSEI held at London’s ExCel, to the comic book and pop culture themed AwesomeCon in Washington.
DSEI, which is held every two years in London as well as in Germany and Japan, has also attracted protests.

Last year, hundreds demonstrated outside the four-day fair in London in protest against Israel’s three biggest arms companies present at the event. Elbit Systems, Rafael and Israel Aerospace Industries have supplied the Israel Defense Forces; the latter two are state-owned.

Clarion’s portfolio also spans travel shows, classic car meet-ups and events for the technology, gaming, design and technology industries. Its Classic Motor Show event in Birmingham next month is billed as the “world’s largest vehicle club gathering”.

blocks.caption: Protests outside the DSEI arms fair last year. Photograph: Jack Taylor/Reuters

blocks.text: Stephen Carter, the Informa chief executive, said the company was “accelerating the focus” on its core live events business, as it also laid out plans to spin off its academic publishing arm, Taylor & Francis.
Informa, which is headquartered in London and employs 14,000 people, hosts big industry events around the world, including London Tech Week and the Cannes Lions International Festival of Creativity.
However the FTSE 100 group’s shares have been flat so far this year as it was forced to reschedule several events in the Middle East because of the conflict in the region.

Last year Carter, who has led the group since 2013, moved his residency from the UK to the UAE and retired from the House of Lords. Informa makes more than a third of its revenue in India, the Middle East and Asia.
after newsletter promotion

The academic publishing business made about $1bn (£760m) last year. Informa said that it had launched a formal process to separate Taylor & Francis, and that it would “review all options”. The outcome of the review will be reported alongside its full-year results in March next year.
Taylor & Francis, which was founded in London in 1852, joined Informa in 2004. It publishes journals and books about science, medicine, technology and engineering.

Informa told investors on Tuesday that in order to fund the Clarion deal, it will raise £940m through a share placing, which will include an offer for armchair investors through the broker RetailBook.

The takeover is expected to accelerate Informa’s growth and bolster its earnings per share from 2027, the company said. Shares in the business, which is listed on the London Stock Exchange, rose by 1.4% in early trading on Tuesday.

articles.title: Germany's ex-spy chief arrested for espionage
articles.summary: August Hanning served as the head of Germany's BND foreign intelligence agency from 1998 to 2005. According to German media, he is being investigated for allegedly passing on state secrets and…

image.caption: August Hanning has reportedly been arrested over alleged spying and acting as a secret service agentImage: Michael Kappeler/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: Police have arrested the former head of Germany's BND foreign intelligence agency, August Hanning, on suspicion of espionage, the federal prosecutor's office announced Tuesday.
Hanning served as the agency's chief between 1998 and 2005.

According to a statement from the prosecutor's office, he is facing charges including alleged espionage against the state, disclosure of state secrets, attempted treason, and working as a secret service agent.

The statement added that a former high-ranking employee of the BND had also been arrested on suspicion of providing Hanning with hundreds of classified documents in exchange for money over more than a decade.
What else do we know about the investigation?
Police arrested Hanning early Tuesday at his home in Nordwalde near the western German city of Münster, according to information from WDR, NDR and the Süddeutsche Zeitung.
Hanning's alleged accomplice, who was identified only as Manfred D. in line with Germany's privacy laws, was taken into custody in Bavaria.
Authorities were conducting searches at both suspects' properties, as well as in Berlin, the prosecutor said.
During Hanning's tenure as spy chief, D. reportedly served as his chief of staff. He is facing charges of aiding and abetting attempted treason and espionage against the state.
More to come...

articles.title: Trump suggests he would let Iran ‘take out’ Los Angeles or San Diego
articles.summary:
Gavin Newsom calls comments ‘deranged and dangerous’ after president tells Nebraska rally: ‘They can take out a city’

Leaders in California have sharply denounced Donald Trump as “reckless”…

blocks.text: Leaders in California have sharply denounced Donald Trump as “reckless” and “deranged” after the US president suggested Iran could “take out” Los Angeles and San Diego – two liberal cities in the blue state that has been a frequent target of his administration.

At a rally in ruby red Nebraska on Monday night, Trump told supporters that he hoped to see a “tremendous victory” in the fast-approaching November midterm elections. He then suggested high prices due to the war with Iran were a “small price to pay for keeping the world safe – keeping our country safe”.
“They can take out a city,” Trump said in Grand Island. “Let them take out Los Angeles. Let them take out San Diego.” The crowd applauded.
“It’ll be over very soon,” Trump said of the war.

The governor and the cities’ mayors quickly condemned the comments. “After sending the National Guard and Marines to occupy California, Donald Trump is now saying our foreign enemies should ‘take out’ Los Angeles and San Diego,” the California governor, Gavin Newsom, said on X. “He is deranged and dangerous.”

Newsom, a Democrat who has repeatedly clashed with Trump over his two terms, said from his press office account: “Let’s be clear: The President is advocating for an attack on 10+ million U.S. residents in two of America’s largest cities. This is not normal. None of this is. And we will continue to remind folks of that every day.”
Karen Bass, the mayor of Los Angeles, assailed the president for making what she called “irresponsible threats” that “could potentially compromise” the safety of America’s second-largest city.
“The role of a president is to protect the country, not to actively threaten it and encourage attacks on American lives,” she said in a statement.

Todd Gloria, the mayor of San Diego, said his city was “not collateral damage” in the president’s war. “We are not expendable. And we are never a “small price to pay,” he wrote on X “Keep our city out of your reckless war talk.”
San Diego, the nation’s eighth-largest city, is home to critical US military infrastructure.

Online, the comments – part of a rambling, nearly hour-and-a-half speech – set off a debate about what the president actually meant. Was it a crude joke about two blue cities or had he, accidentally perhaps, disclosed confidential intelligence about potential Iranian targets?

Some conservative activists argued that Trump, in his elliptical way of speaking, was referring to high gas prices when he argued that it was a “small price to pay”, and not the capacity of Iran to “take out” a US city.
The White House did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
US defence officials have previously stated that Iran currently lacks the capability to launch a direct missile attack on the US mainland.

Trump has argued in previous speeches that allowing Iran to develop a nuclear weapon would threaten US cities. In his last state of the union speech he claimed that Iran was working to build missiles that would “soon” reach US soil.

In Nebraska, where an unexpectedly close Senate race has rattled Republicans, Trump insisted that he was “doing great” and urged supporters to pretend like his name was on the ballot when the vote in November. But in California, where Steve Hilton, the Republican gubernatorial candidate endorsed by Trump, is seeking an upset, the president’s comments were unwelcome.

“Thirteen million Californians call LA and San Diego counties home,” said Xavier Becerra, the Democratic nominee for governor who has sought to take up the anti-Trump mantle carried by the outgoing Newsom. “Their lives are not a ‘small price to pay’ or a punchline for Donald Trump.”

articles.title: Boy recounts 1994 park attack on tape played at trial of alleged sex predator
articles.summary: Thirty-two years after a 10-year-old boy was tied to a tree and sexually assaulted, an audio tape of his September 1994 police interview was played for the jury Monday at the trial of his alleged…

image.caption: In September 1994, Peel Regional Police said a boy was walking through Brampton's Norton Place Park, when he was approached by a suspect and lured to a nearby wooded area where he was sexually assaulted. Thirty-two years later, an audio recording of the boy's interview with police was played for the

blocks.text: Toronto·New

Thirty-two years after a 10-year-old boy was tied to a tree and sexually assaulted, an audio tape of his September 1994 police interview was played for the jury Monday at the trial of his alleged attacker. Richard Neil has pleaded not guilty to 17 historical charges linked to attacks on three children.
Richard Neil has pleaded not guilty to 17 historical charges, including kidnapping, sexual assault
WARNING: This article contains graphic content and may affect those who have experienced​ ​​​sexual violence or know someone affected by it.
As police drove him to Toronto's Hospital for Sick Children, the 10-year-old boy kept asking if they were nearly there.
"My stomach's turning," he told the two officers, as he lay in the back of the vehicle.

Thirty-two years after the child was tied to a tree and sexually assaulted, an audio recording of his September 1994 interview with police was played for the jury Monday at the trial of his alleged attacker.

Richard Neil has pleaded not guilty to 17 charges related to the incident, as well as two other similar past attacks on an eight-year-old boy and a 15-year-old girl. The list of allegations includes kidnapping, sexual assault causing bodily harm and administering a stupefying drug.

The three attacks in southern Ontario parks between 1992 and 1995 confounded investigators for three decades. Advances in DNA technology — including investigative genetic genealogy — finally helped police link the three crime scenes to Neil, a prosecutor told the jury Monday in the Ontario Superior Court of Justice in Brampton, Ont.
Neil, now 67, was arrested in 2024.
The court heard the former postal worker doesn't dispute what happened to the three children, but insists he wasn't involved.
"He did a lot of rude things to me," the 10-year-old boy told Peel Regional Police about the unidentified attacker in 1994.

The victim, whose identity is covered by a publication ban, recounted saying hello to a stranger in Brampton's Norton Place Park after school that day. They struck up a conversation. The man claimed he had lost his wallet with $900 inside.

items: Crown says DNA evidence helped ID man now on trial for decades-old sex assaults against children

blocks.text: The boy said the pair walked around the park and chatted on a bench, until the man's mood suddenly soured, ostensibly accusing the boy of stealing his wallet.
"He tied my foot to the tree ... so I couldn't get away," the boy is heard telling police on the audio tape.
He described a series of lurid acts carried out by the man in a wooded area of the park, including urination, oral sex and anal penetration.
"It hurt," the boy told police.
After the attacker got away, the boy ran out of the woods, exiting near a branch of the Royal Canadian Legion adjacent to the park.
Witness recalls seeing boy run from park
David Kilpatrick, now a 71-year-old retiree, testified Monday about stopping at the Legion that evening to have a beer and play a round of pool.
Everything changed when he spotted the child wearing only his pants.
"I see this young boy coming out of the woods … shirt in hand, screaming, so I knew something was wrong," Kilpatrick told the court.
"You have to call my mom," he said the boy urged him. "I've been attacked."
Kilpatrick said the boy provided a basic description of the attacker: a white man with black hair, wearing a grey track suit.
He ran the boy into the Legion, told the bartender to call 911 and rushed into the woods himself to find the assailant, to no avail.
Kilpatrick fought back tears Monday as he spoke from the witness box. He said he promised the 10-year-old that day he would find his attacker.
"I was wound up like a clock," he told the court. "Still am, just talking about it now."
DNA tied 3 assaults to 1 man: Crown

That evening, the boy led investigators to the spot where he'd been attacked. DNA recovered from the Brampton park — as well as semen and men's underwear worn as a mask, each found separately at the scenes of two other assaults — proved crucial in linking the three incidents to one man, Crown attorney Shazin Karim told the jury.

In the first attack at Kitchener's Idlewood Park on Aug. 21, 1992, a boy said he'd been lured away from his sister and a friend by a man who promised to show him dozens of bicycles in a wooded area, Karim said.
She told the jury the assailant held a pocket knife and threatened to kill the eight-year-old "if he said a word."

On Aug. 31, 1995, at Oakville's Wildwood Park, a girl out walking her dog was approached by a man who threatened her with what appeared to be a loaded gun, Karim told the court in her opening statement. She said the 15-year-old cried as the man set up a video camera to record the assault.

articles.title: Giant underwater Kelvin wave could 'pack a punch' for B.C. in mid-October
articles.summary: A giant underwater wave of water connected to this year's El Niño weather pattern is making its way up the west coast of the Americas, raising alarm bells amongst scientists worried about how climate…

image.caption: Waves and debris crash into the breakwater in Victoria, B.C. in 2024. This year's El Niño will soon send more waves at B.C.'s coast. (Chad Hipolito/The Canadian Press)

blocks.text: Science

A giant underwater wave of water connected to this year's El Niño weather pattern is making its way up the west coast of the Americas, raising alarm bells amongst scientists worried about how climate change is magnifying the impacts of the naturally-occurring phenomenon.
El Niño phenomenon could worsen the effects of storm surges and high tides
· CBC News
· Posted: Oct 06, 2026 4:00 AM EDT | Last Updated: 31 minutes ago

A giant underwater wave of water connected to this year's El Niño weather pattern is moving up the west coast of the Americas, raising alarm bells among scientists about how climate change is magnifying the impacts of the naturally occurring phenomenon.
The so-called Kelvin wave is not unexpected. But like El Niño as a whole, it is happening on top of human-caused climate change that has already warmed the oceans and atmosphere.

A smaller wave already reached B.C. earlier this summer, and the next one is expected to arrive within one to two weeks, according to Bill Merryfield, a research scientist at Environment and Climate Change Canada.
"We actually did already see over 30 centimetres in some locations in June. And so the coming wave looks like it'll be a stronger one," Merryfield said.
What causes it?

The Kelvin wave is a naturally occurring weather phenomenon, just like El Niño itself. In normal years, winds blow from east to west along the equator in the Pacific Ocean, generally pushing water from South America toward Asia.
During El Niño years, however, those east-to-west winds weaken or can reverse direction, allowing water to move east instead.

"When these Kelvin waves reach the coast of South America, there's nowhere further east for this pile up of water to go. And so it splits and starts running up and down the coasts of the Americas" and eventually all the way up to Canada, Merryfield said.
Sea-level monitoring data collected at Tofino, on Vancouver Island's Pacific coast, shows the impact of the earlier Kelvin wave in June.
Rather than a giant tsunami-like wave, the Kelvin wave temporarily raises sea levels.

"You can think of it more like a very broad, hundreds of miles wide, but very shallow bulge in the height of the ocean surface, so by maybe a foot or so," University of California climate scientist Daniel Swain told CBS News last month.
What will it do to the West Coast?
Merryfield said the impacts are most pronounced during king tides, particularly high tides that happen when the gravitational pull of the sun and moon combine to produce higher-than-normal tides.

"So if you put that 30 centimetres of sea level rise on top of a king tide, and then maybe you add a winter storm to that, which causes a storm surge, that's when you really start to get into trouble," he said.
"This extra foot or so of sea level rise due to El Niño can pack a punch."
El Niño-fuelled heat could kill half a million people by February: study

Those surges could be intensified by another effect of El Niño, further raising sea levels along the B.C coast. El Niño can strengthen northward winds along the coast, pushing even more water toward shore.

These compounding effects — the Kelvin wave, stronger northward winds and winter storms, on top of climate change already raising sea levels and intensifying extreme weather — could worsen flooding and erosion along the coast. Strong El Niños in the past have caused widespread erosion on California's beaches.
Local authorities there are placing emergency sand on beaches and expect the Kelvin wave to raise water levels six to 12 inches, the Associated Press reports.
The impacts of the Kelvin wave — and El Niño more broadly — could extend far beyond this season, Merryfield warned.

The oceans absorb much of the excess heat trapped by greenhouse gases, moderating global warming as humans continue to burn fossil fuels. During El Niños, however, some of that stored heat is released from the ocean into the atmosphere.
This will likely lead to 2027 becoming the warmest year on record "by quite a significant margin," Merryfield said, echoing similar warnings from other climate research organizations and scientists.
ABOUT THE AUTHOR
Inayat Singh covers the environment and climate change at CBC News. He is based in Toronto and has previously reported from Winnipeg. Email: inayat.singh@cbc.ca

articles.title: Whey up: Protein powder prices soar as global demand grows
articles.summary: Food manufacturers and fast food companies are cramming whey protein into everything. That’s causing shortages of the ingredient and pushing prices to record highs. Now whey protein is also a target…

image.caption: How counter-tariffs on the U.S. could backfire on Canadian whey protein companies (CBC News)

blocks.text: Business

Food manufacturers and fast food companies are cramming whey protein into everything. That’s causing shortages of the ingredient and pushing prices to record highs. Now whey protein is also a target in the U.S.-Canada trade war - increasing costs that may end up being passed on to customers.
Consumers, companies feel squeeze of supply shortage

Jennifer Mason is trying to eat more protein and has supplemented her diet with whey protein powder over the past few years. But lately, soaring prices are giving her sticker shock. And as a new mom with rising expenses, she's rethinking her shopping list.
"I'm just cutting back. I'm trying to find protein in whole foods that I'm eating rather than actually getting products," she says.

To meet growing demand, food manufacturers and fast food companies are putting whey protein into everything from snacks to drinks. That's contributing to shortages of the ingredient and pushing prices to record highs. Now whey protein is also caught in the U.S.-Canada trade war, increasing costs that may end up being passed on to consumers.
Protein on the menu

From chips and Pop-Tarts to candy, protein-packed foods are popping up on grocery store shelves. Khloé Kardashian recently launched protein popcorn. Starbucks is offering protein cold foam, catching up with the whey protein shots on the menu at Booster Juice.

Major brands are adding whey protein to their products to appeal to health-conscious consumers. Fitness influencers are pushing protein-maxxing, a trend of consuming dietary protein at every opportunity. And as more people take weight-loss drugs like Ozempic, some are also eating more protein to prevent muscle loss.
It's all eating into the global supply of whey protein concentrate, one of the most popular ingredients used in high-protein foods.

John Murray manages marketing for Daryl's Bars, a protein snack manufacturer in Tecumseh, Ont. He says as major companies secure large orders of whey, "that leaves the little guys like us scrambling to try and secure enough for our operations."
Canada imports most of its whey protein concentrate from the U.S., where prices have more than doubled over the past year and a half.
The U.S. Dairy Export Council says "domestic demand for high-protein whey has been insatiable" — so much so, that less whey is available for export.
That demand has also driven up prices. Whey protein concentrate, known as WPC80, rose 60 per cent in 2025. By June 2026, buyers were facing another 76 per cent increase.
To keep up with rising costs, Murray says his company has been forced to raise prices on its protein snacks.
"We absorbed as much as we could, but over the last year it's just been impossible. It's been outstripping our margins completely," he said.
Most of the company's whey protein comes from Wisconsin, and Murray says there are few alternatives.
"If we could source 100 per cent of everything that we needed from inside Canada, we would opt for that."
Caught in the trade war
The trade war is further squeezing food manufacturers.
In retaliation for a fresh round of U.S. tariffs on Canadian goods, the federal government imposed 50 per cent tariffs on imports of American whey on Sept. 8, pushing prices even higher.
Canadian businesses can apply for relief through Ottawa's tariff-remission program, though they must demonstrate that the goods cannot reasonably be sourced domestically or from non-U.S. suppliers.

It will be difficult to boost supply quickly, said Mike von Massow, a food economist at the University of Guelph, because whey isn't produced on its own. It's a byproduct left over from making cheese. The liquid whey must be dried and turned into a powder, a complex process that requires special equipment.
"It's very expensive to dry something that is 95 per cent water and a little bit of protein," he said.
How counter-tariffs on the U.S. could backfire on Canadian whey protein companies
The U.S. produces a lot of cheese, which is why it's also a major producer of whey protein. But von Massow says Canada has limited processing capacity.
"We can't produce milk just for the whey. That's not economic. Even though the price is up, the rest of the milk would be a byproduct," he said.

The Dairy Processors Association of Canada says that with tariffs increasing the cost of U.S. imports, it expects Canadian companies to pivot toward New Zealand — though that comes with significant shipping costs.
Stretching their dollars
Von Massow predicts higher prices could be passed down through the supply chain.
"I think your protein drink is probably going to get more expensive and it's likely to stay more expensive for a while," he said.
Some protein users, such as Audrey Marcoux, say they will absorb the extra cost for now.
"Unfortunately, I'm still paying the more expensive price because it's part of my routine. I work out a lot," she said.
Nathan Bugiardini says that if prices go any higher, he'll consider cutting back.
"It's a little upsetting, frankly. I usually buy in bulk which helps the price a little bit."
Some consumers are turning to plant-based alternatives and unprocessed whole foods while whey protein prices remain high.
Nineteen-year-old Melania Antic says the steep costs have left her feeling stretched.
"It discourages me a lot, especially, like, to actually get motivation to go to the gym and take protein after."
ABOUT THE AUTHOR

Nisha Patel is a senior reporter with CBC News. She's covered business and economics for more than a decade and spends her days talking to economists, CEOs, policymakers and everyday people to make sense of complex stories. You can find her on X at @nishapatel or by email at nisha.patel@cbc.ca.

blocks.text: Toronto·New
Self-described "Crypto King" Aiden Pleterski's fraud and money laundering trial will begin Tuesday morning in Toronto.
Jury of 7 men, 7 women selected Monday afternoon
Self-described "Crypto King" Aiden Pleterski's criminal trial will begin Tuesday morning in Toronto.
Pleterski, 27, pleaded not guilty to fraud of over $5,000 and money laundering ahead of jury selection in Ontario Superior Court on Monday.
He’s representing himself at trial.

A jury of seven men and seven women was selected Monday afternoon. Justice Shaun Nakatsuru decided on 14 people, given the trial is expected to last a month. However, only 12 jurors will deliberate at the end of the case.

Pleterski was arrested in May 2024, after a lengthy joint investigation by Durham Regional Police and the Ontario Securities Commission dubbed Project Swan. Police alleged Pleterski operated a multimillion-dollar fraud scheme with funds he received from investors between July 2020 and the end of July 2022.

CBC Toronto has reported extensively on Pleterski since the summer of 2022, when he was forced into bankruptcy by some of his investors trying to recover millions of dollars they gave him to invest in cryptocurrency and foreign exchange.
Crown prosecutors are expected to call more than a dozen witnesses over the course of the trial.

articles.summary: Bicol Saro Party-List Representative Terry Ridon on Tuesday said there was no conflict of interest on his part for participating in the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte as a House…

blocks.text: Published October 6, 2026 3:49pm

Bicol Saro Party-List Representative Terry Ridon on Tuesday said there was no conflict of interest on his part for participating in the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte as a House Prosecutor despite his prior position as consultant for the Davao City Government.
Ridon said he was never a personal adviser to then Davao City Mayor Sara Duterte and instead provided policy consultancy services on poverty alleviation.

“We performed the work required under the engagement and submitted the corresponding reports to the City Government. The consultancy was never subject to any audit disallowance, more than six years after the engagement concluded,” he said in a statement.

“So what exactly is the supposed conflict of interest? My responsibility today is different and clear: as a prosecutor, I will present the evidence before the Senate Impeachment Court. The Court will determine the merits of the allegations,” he added.
Ridon said the prosecution will not be distracted from its presentation of evidence under unexplained wealth.
In a separate press briefing, Duterte said she knew about his consultancy services but did not divulge them as she wanted him to say that he had a conflict of interest.
She claimed that Ridon did provide work but received wages for it.
“‘Yun pala wala siyang gagawin kung hindi tatanggap lang ng pera. And may evidence ang City Treasurer Office na na-remit sa Land Bank Account niya ‘yung lump sum ng kanyang consultancy,” she said.
(It turns out he had nothing to do except receive money. And the City Treasurer’s Office has evidence that the lump sum for his consultancy was remitted to his Land Bank account.)

“Dapat kapag consultant ka meron kang ambag, meron kang accomplishment na nakatulong ka sa pang gobyerno. So nung ni-review na namin nakita namin this person walang ginawa, tumanggap ng pera. Alisin na ‘yan diyan,” she later added.

(If you are a consultant, you should have a contribution; you should have accomplishments showing that you helped the government. So when we reviewed it, we saw that this person did nothing, received money. Remove him from there.) — BAP, GMA News

blocks.text: Vice President Sara Duterte on Tuesday said her mother, Elizabeth Zimmerman, has asked her to return to local politics instead of running for a national position in the 2028 elections.
Duterte also said that her mother floated the idea of Davao Mayor Sebastian “Baste” Duterte, her brother, running for a national post.
“Nagsabi talaga ‘yung nanay ko na pinapauwi niya ako ng Davao at si Baste na lang ang patakbuhin sa national elections,” she said.
(My mother really said that she wanted me to return to Davao and that Baste should be the one to run in the national elections.)
She was asked if she was considering fielding Baste Duterte for a national position as an alternative for her in the elections following her brother's testimony before the Senate impeachment court.
“Sa pamilya namin ‘yun lang ang napag-usapan… Hindi napagusapan.... Sinabi ng nanay ko, sabi niya umuwi ka dito sa Davao tapos bahala na si Baste diyan sa national,” she said.

(In our family, that was the only thing that was discussed… It wasn’t discussed. It was said. My mother said it. She said, “Come home here to Davao, then let Baste handle things there at the national level.”)

“Wala pa akong iniisip na tao na sasabihin ko na tumakbo ka. Sa tingin ko sa ugali ko naman, wala akong sasabihan na tumakbo ka,” she added... Kasi para sa akin, and personal experience ko ito, ang pagtakbo talaga dapat personal na desisyon," she added.

(I haven’t thought of anyone whom I would tell to run. I think, given my personality, I wouldn’t tell anyone to run. For me, and this is based on my personal experience, running for office should really be a personal decision. First of all, the job is not easy. Second, campaigning and elections are not easy.)
Castro reacts
Palace Press Officer Undersecretary Claire Castro, meanwhile, had a reaction to Duterte's statements asking the Vice President to "work first" before thinking of the national elections.
"Trabaho muna para sa mga kababayan natin ang unahin hindi puro pangangampanya para mai-angat ang mga sarili," Castro said.
(Prioritize working for our fellow citizens first, rather than focusing solely on campaigning to advance one's own interests.)

"Wala na ngang naitutulong sa bayan, nakakabigat pa sa ekonomiya ang mga taong puro paninira lang ang alam. Ang totoong public servant...masipag umaksyon para sa bayan...hindi pwedeng walang alam ang laging panangga sa ibinabatong anomalya sa kanya," she added.

(People who do nothing but badmouth others not only fail to contribute to the nation but also become a burden on the economy. A true public servant is proactive in working for the country; one cannot simply be clueless when defending oneself against allegations of wrongdoing.)

Duterte is the subject of an impeachment trial, where she is accused of committing grave threats against President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. and others, misuse of confidential funds, unexplained wealth, and bribery.
She is also facing three counts of grave threats before a Quezon City court.
Duterte said that President Ferdinand “Bongbong” Marcos Jr. and his administration are behind the allegations against her.
“Administrasyon. Sino ang nasa likod ng paninira sa akin? Administrasyon. Ang Palasyo, si BBM,” Duterte said.
(The administration. Who is behind the smear campaign against me? The administration. The Palace, BBM.)
Castro said the allegations against Duterte are her own making.
“Sila ang nakinabang sa bawat sentimo na nakukuha nila o nadedeposito sa kanilang account ng mga banyaga at diumano'y drug lords,” she said.
(They are the ones who benefited from every centavo they received or that was allegedly deposited into their accounts by foreigners and alleged drug lords.)

In September, dismissed policeman Rodulfo Gracioso Jr. claimed that he delivered cash to her, Davao City 1st District Representative Paolo Duterte, and former President Rodrigo Duterte on former House Speaker Lord Allan Velasco’s instructions.
Duterte has denied the allegations against her.
Velasco’s camp, meanwhile, said the allegations against him had “no basis.” —VAL, GMA News

Duterte issued the remark amid the claims of dismissed policeman Rodulfo Gracioso Jr. that she received suitcases of cash from former House Speaker Lord Allan Velasco.

articles.title: FACT CHECK: Marcos Jr. did not say protecting VP Duterte from her case is ‘corruption’
articles.summary: A viral Facebook graphic attributes a statement to President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. about Vice President Sara Duterte’s legal troubles, but the official transcript of Marcos’ media briefing in India…

blocks.text: Claim: President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. said he could not be blamed for Sara Duterte’s legal troubles, that he could not protect her from her case, and that if a president did so, “corruption” would be the result.
Why we fact-checked this: A viral Facebook graphic posted by Senior Rak Joe, a Facebook page with around 15,000 followers, attributes a statement to President Ferdinand Marcos Jr.
It claims that Marcos made the statement on September 13, 2026, amid his remarks about Vice President Sara Duterte. It had garnered around 102,000 views as of October 5, 2026.

The graphic says, “Yung pinanggalingan ng kaso niya galing mismo sa bibig niya, kilos at galaw niya, di niya ako pwedeng sisihin kung ano man ang mga nararanasan niyang pagsubok… Ano gusto niya gawin ko, protektahan ko siya sa kaso? Di naman pwede ’yun. Kung gagawin ng isang Presidente ’yan, corruption pa rin ang kalalabasan niyan…”

(The case against her stemmed from her own words, actions, and conduct. She cannot blame me for whatever challenges she is going through. What does she want me to do, protect her from the case? That’s not possible. If a president were to do that, it would still amount to corruption.)
On September 13, the President was in New Delhi, India, for the Philippines’ participation in the 18th BRICS Summit. He also held a Kapihan with the Media at the Taj Mahal Hotel.

The facts: On September 13, during a Kapihan with the Media, Marcos was asked about his thoughts on the issues surrounding the Vice President. In that press conference, the President did not say the quoted statement in the Facebook post.

The official transcript of his Kapihan remarks contains no statement saying that Duterte’s case came “from her own mouth,” that he could not be blamed for her situation, that he was being asked to protect her from the case, or that doing so would constitute “corruption.”
What Marcos Jr. actually said was, “You know, I hear about them, but I don’t really even have a response. If she feels very angry, I suppose, with what’s happening to her.”
“And I am the target of that anger, or the main target of that anger. What can I do? You cannot force anyone to love you,” he added.
The phrase “wala siya sa tamang pag-iisip” (she’s not in her right mind) also does not appear in his Kapihan remarks.
A similar remark, however, was made by Presidential Communications Office Undersecretary and Palace Press Officer Claire Castro during a September 11 press briefing in New Delhi.
While responding to Duterte’s statements, Castro asked, “Nasa tama ba siyang huwisyo? Nasa tama ba siyang pag-iisip?” (Is she in her right mind? Is she thinking clearly?)

Castro was referring to Duterte’s state of mind after the Vice President made statements against Marcos Jr. She also referred to “sleepless nights and anxiety” as possible factors affecting Duterte’s statements. – Ahyenne Neleah Estacio/Rappler.com

Keep us aware of suspicious Facebook pages, groups, accounts, websites, articles, or photos in your network by contacting us at factcheck@rappler.com. Let us battle disinformation one Fact Check at a time.

Ahyenne Neleah Estacio is a graduating Bachelor of Arts in Communication student and campus journalist at Holy Angel University. The current senior editor and former editor-in-chief of The Angelite, she is an Aries Rufo Fellow for 2026.

articles.title: Taylor’s hardline immigration plan drags Australian politics further to the right – and it’s all upside for One Nation
articles.summary:
Coalition leader’s proposal goes further than Peter Dutton’s 2025 election promise and beyond even Pauline Hanson’s bottom line

  • Get our

blocks.text: With Angus Taylor’s hardline immigration policy unveiled on Tuesday, voters have a new measure of Pauline Hanson’s success in dragging politics further to the right.

Taylor’s plan will cut 60,000 more people from net overseas migration (Nom) than the reductions proposed by Peter Dutton just before the 2025 election. Dutton wanted to take Nom down to about 160,000 people a year, while Taylor’s plan goes far further, beyond even Hanson’s bottom line of 130,000 people.
In the nearly 18 months since the poll, Hanson’s surge in support has coincided with intense focus on the Nom, previously a fairly unremarkable budget forecast which came and went each year.

Based on sometimes scant economic analysis, the three parties – which current polling shows have a chance of forming government after the next election – have all introduced plans to cut Nom, targeting overseas arrivals increasingly seen by voters as clogging up essential infrastructure, taking houses or rorting the rules.
Taylor proudly called his plan “the largest cut to immigration in Australian history”.

It would reduce the number of temporary visa holders by about 650,000 people over four years. From the 100,000 level in the first and second years of a Coalition government, Nom would grow to 130,000 arrivals in year three and 160,000 in year four.

Taylor has met the demands of Nationals MPs and left plenty of space for the working holidaymakers needed to pick fruit and work in rural and regional hospitality. He used the announcement to take a swipe at the country’s university sector, claiming one of Australia’s biggest exports sells visa pathways, not higher education.
Humanitarian visa places would be slashed to 10,000 under the Coalition, a 50% cut from Labor’s cap of 20,000 people a year.

But serious questions remain. The immigration expert Alan Gamlen, of Australian National University, says achieving cuts of this scale would be difficult for an incoming government and would certainly result in economic losers.

It is unclear how skilled visas, currently a demand-driven aspect of the immigration scheme, could be increased by about 100,000 people in select industries, as Taylor proposes. Labor believes the only way to increase uncapped visa numbers would be to allow migrants to arrive without a job offer.

Eliminating bridging visas may be much more difficult – and expensive – than Taylor imagines. Migrants seeking permanent residency, skilled work or family rights often await processing on bridging visas. How would this caseload be managed?
Taylor’s plan fell flat with business and asylum seeker advocates.
after newsletter promotion

Speaking for big business, a traditional Coalition constituency, the Australian Chamber of Commerce and Industry boss, Andrew McKellar, said chasing arbitrary Nom targets was misguided and would hurt the economy.
“Business rejects the false binary that Australia must choose either fewer migrants with higher skills or more migrants with lower skills,” he said.

Responding to news the Coalition plan would halve Australia’s already grudging humanitarian intake, the Asylum Seeker Resource Centre’s Jana Favero said Taylor was out of touch with everyday Australians.
“Instead of focusing on the real problems – how to help people pay their rent, manage their mortgage or put food on the table – the Coalition is joining the far right’s blame game,” she said.

The politics of immigration remains all upside for Hanson, who has Taylor and the prime minister, Anthony Albanese, on the back foot. On Tuesday, she said the major parties had to be dragged kicking and screaming to their cuts, and claimed they couldn’t be trusted to deliver anyway.
Whoever voters decide they best trust on immigration, the centre has dramatically shifted in One Nation’s favour. Where it stays could change the country.
